evidence.ML_ANOMALY: Statistical anomaly signal. Informational only; review required.
evidence.DEED_NO_FORMAT_INVALID: Possible inconsistency: deed number “{deedNo}” does not look like a registry deed number. Review required.
evidence.IMPOSSIBLE_DATE: {reason, select, FUTURE {Possible inconsistency: a transfer is dated {date}, which is in the future. evidence.RAPID_RESALE: Possible inconsistency: the seller held the parcel for only {heldDays} days (recorded {acquiredOn}) before the transfer on {date}. Review required.
evidence.ACTIVE_LITIGATION: Recorded: an active court case ({referenceNo}) is attached to this parcel. Review required.
evidence.KHAS_LAND: Recorded: this parcel is listed as khas (government) land ({referenceNo}). Review required.
evidence.UNDER_ACQUISITION: Recorded: an active acquisition ({referenceNo}) is attached to this parcel. Review required.
evidence.ACTIVE_MORTGAGE: Recorded: an active mortgage ({referenceNo}) is attached to this parcel. Informational.
evidence.RECORD_INTEGRITY_FAILED: Potential inconsistency: a record of this parcel differs from the ledger entry written when it was approved. Review required.
evidence.SURVEY_CHAIN_GAP: Possible inconsistency: {unlinked} of {owners} owner(s) in the {toSurvey} survey record have no recorded link to the {fromSurvey} survey holders. Review required.
evidence.HISTORICAL_CHAIN_GAP: Possible inconsistency: the buyer in the {date} historical deed has no recorded link to the owners of the later {toSurvey} khatian (the seller matches the {fromSurvey} khatian). Review required.
evidence.HISTORICAL_SELLER_NOT_OWNER: Possible inconsistency: the seller in the {date} historical deed does not match any owner in the CS / SA khatian of this parcel. Review required.
evidence.HISTORICAL_DAG_CONFLICT: {basis, select, DAG {Possible inconsistency: the historical deed of {date} conveys dag {dags}, already conveyed by the deed of {earlierDate}, and its seller is not linked to that deed's buyer. Review required.} other {Possible inconsistency: the historical deed of {date} conveys the same khatian as the deed of {earlierDate}, and its seller is not linked to that deed's buyer. Review required.}}
evidence.HISTORICAL_CONSIDERATION_IMPLAUSIBLE: {reason, select, CURRENCY_ERA {Possible inconsistency: the price in the {date} historical deed is written in {currency}, which does not fit the era of the deed. about.title: About LandShield BD
about.intro: A civic-tech prototype built on synthetic data. It supports human reviewers and never makes a legal determination.

purpose.title: Purpose
purpose.body: LandShield BD shows how digital record organisation, consistency checks and transparent risk indicators could help people and reviewers examine land records before a transaction.

limits.title: Limitations
limits.l1: It is a prototype and has not been tested on real records.
limits.l2: Text extraction can be wrong; every document needs human review.
limits.l3: Risk indicators point to potential inconsistencies and can be false alarms.
limits.l4: It does not cover every kind of land record or every legal situation.

demo.title: Sample data
demo.body: Every parcel, owner and document in this site is synthetic. Any resemblance to real records is accidental.

notice.title: Not legal advice
notice.body: LandShield does not establish legal ownership, certify title or replace official government or legal verification. Consult the relevant authority or a qualified lawyer before acting on any land transaction.

errors.SPOUSE_BOTH: A husband and wives cannot both be heirs of the same person.
errors.COUNT_RANGE: Counts must be whole numbers from 0 to 30.

notes.awl: The fixed shares added up to more than the whole, so every share was reduced in proportion (awl).
notes.radd: There was no residuary heir, so the remainder returned to the sharers other than a spouse (radd).
notes.umar: Mother takes one third of what remains after the spouse (the two-parents-and-spouse rule).
notes.excluded: Siblings are excluded by a son or the father.
notes.leftover: Part of the estate is not assigned to any listed heir. Other relatives or the state may be entitled.
notes.scope: Not covered: grandparents, grandchildren, half-siblings, wills, missing persons, other religions.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.purpose: Short answers about what LandShield BD does and does not do.

q1.a: A demonstration web app that shows how digital land-record checks, document verification and risk indicators could work. It runs on synthetic sample data.

q2.q: Is this an official government service?
q2.a: No. It is not a government system and its results are not official land records. It has no connection to any land office.

q3.q: Which land records does it contain?
q3.a: Only invented parcels, owners and documents created for the demo. See the Data sources page for the full list.

q4.q: How do I check a plot?
q4.a: Choose "Verify land", pick the district and upazila, then enter the mouza, khatian and dag number. You see the recorded details, history and risk indicators.

q5.q: What does the risk level mean?
q5.a: It counts fixed consistency rules that did not match, for example a seller who is not the recorded owner. It points a reviewer to look closer; it is not a finding of fraud.

q6.q: Can I rely on it before buying land?
q6.a: No. Use it only to learn what a check can show. Before any purchase, get official verification from the relevant authority and advice from a qualified lawyer.

q7.q: Why does every document need human review?
q7.a: Text read from a scan can be wrong, especially in Bangla handwriting or poor images. An officer must confirm the extracted fields before a record is approved.

q8.a: No for the public pages: checking a copy, tracking a mutation, the tools and the map overview. Officers and reviewers sign in to work on records.

q9.q: How do I change the language or text size?
q9.a: Use the language switch and the text-size buttons in the top bar. Your choice is remembered in this browser.

accessibility.title: Accessibility statement
accessibility.purpose: What we have built in so far, what is still weak, and how to tell us.

s1.title: What is in place
s1.body: We aim to meet WCAG 2.1 level AA. These are the features you can use today:

items.i1: Bangla first, with English one click away
items.i2: Text-size buttons and a light or dark theme in the top bar
items.i3: Full keyboard use, a visible focus ring and a skip-to-content link
items.i4: Touch targets of at least 44 px
items.i5: Status shown by icon and text, never by colour alone

s2.title: Known gaps
s2.body: This is a student demo and has not had a full audit with assistive technology. Known gaps:

items.i1: The interactive map is mainly visual; the place menu and search give the same places as text
items.i2: Charts have text summaries nearby but not full data tables everywhere
items.i3: Bangla text from scanned documents may be misread by OCR
items.i4: PDF reports have not been tested with screen readers

s3.title: Tell us about a problem
s3.body: If something does not work for you, email support@landshield.demo with the page address and what happened. This is a demo address with no guaranteed reply time.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.purpose: What this demo stores about you and why.

s1.title: What we store
s1.body: Public pages need no account and do not ask for personal details. Signed-in staff accounts and their work create these records:

items.i1: Account: name, email address, role and preferred language
items.i2: Documents an officer uploads and the fields extracted from them
items.i3: An audit log of who did what, in which role, and when

s2.title: Browser storage
s2.body: We keep only what the site needs to work:

items.i1: Your theme, text size and language
items.i2: A flag that you signed in on this browser, and a sign-in cookie that scripts cannot read

s3.title: Third parties
s3.body: The map loads background tiles from OpenStreetMap, so that service can see your IP address and the area you view. Nothing else is sent to other companies.

s4.title: Demo data
s4.body: All parcels, owners and documents are synthetic. Do not upload real documents or real personal data. The hosted demo may be reset at any time, which deletes everything stored in it.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.purpose: The conditions for using this demonstration.

s1.title: Demonstration only
s1.body: LandShield BD is a prototype built on synthetic data. It is not a government system and does not create, change or certify any real land record.

s2.title: Please do not
s2.body: Use of the site is at your own risk. You agree not to:

items.i1: Rely on a result as legal proof of ownership or title
items.i2: Upload real personal or confidential documents
items.i3: Scrape, overload or probe the service or its data
items.i4: Try to bypass sign-in, roles or rate limits

s3.title: No legal advice
s3.body: Risk indicators and checks help a person look closer. They are not a legal opinion. Consult the relevant authority or a qualified lawyer before acting on a land transaction.

s4.title: Licence and warranty
s4.body: The source code is released under the MIT licence. Third-party data and fonts keep their own licences. The service is provided as is, without any warranty.

dataSources.title: Data sources
dataSources.purpose: Where every dataset in this demo comes from.

s1.title: Land records
s1.body: All land, deed and person records are synthetic and invented for this demo. No khatian, deed, owner or plot data was read from any government land-record system.

s2.title: Open data we use
s2.body: Third-party data is simplified and not official:

items.i1: Division, district and upazila boundaries: geoBoundaries (CC BY 4.0) through the bangladesh-geojson project (ODbL)
items.i3: Fonts: GNU FreeSans for generated PDFs

s3.title: Government portals
s3.body: The app and its scripts do not contact any government portal. An earlier version held data collected from such portals; it was removed and nothing from them remains.

s4.title: Tools that read documents
s4.body: Text is read from uploads by Tesseract OCR. An optional AI model can help parse fields when it is switched on. In every case a human reviews the result before approval.

items.i2: Claude by Anthropic (optional, off unless a key is set)

verify.title: Verify land
verify.intro: Use the khatian and dag numbers to see if the land is on record. You also see whether it has a case or other claims.

s1.title: Choose the area
s1.body: Open Verify land. Pick the district and upazila from the lists. Then type the mouza name.
s1.alt: Verify land page with the district, upazila and mouza fields outlined.

s2.title: Enter the khatian and dag numbers
s2.body: Type the khatian number and the dag number. Bangla or English digits both work. Then press Verify.
s2.alt: Khatian and dag fields filled in, with the Verify button outlined.

s3.title: Read the short result
s3.body: The result shows how many owners there are and whether there is a case. Sign in to see the full report.
s3.alt: Short result card: number of owners, open case and claims.

check.title: Check before you buy
check.intro: Look for warning signs before you buy land. Take the list to the land office or a lawyer.

s1.title: Sign in
s1.body: This service needs a citizen account. If you do not have one, register for free.
s1.alt: Citizen sign-in page with the email and password fields outlined.

s2.title: Enter the land details
s2.body: Give the area, khatian and dag numbers. Add the seller's name if you know it. Then press Run checklist.
s2.alt: Check before you buy form filled in, with the Run checklist button outlined.

s3.title: Read the indicators
s3.body: Each row says Clear, Review or Indicator. If you see an indicator, get advice before you pay anyone.
s3.alt: Checklist with a red indicator on the khas land row.

track.title: Mutation status
track.intro: See which stage your mutation application has reached. You only need the application number.

s1.title: Open the mutation tab
s1.body: On the home page search card, press Mutation status. The page is also in the Services menu.
s1.alt: Home page search card with the Mutation status tab outlined.

s2.title: Enter the application number
s2.body: Type the mutation number from your receipt, for example MUT-2023-0007. Then press Track status.
s2.alt: Application number typed in, with the Track status button outlined.

s3.title: Follow the stages
s3.body: You see four stages: applied, review, hearing and decision. Finished stages have a tick and a date.
s3.alt: The four mutation stages with their state and date.

verifyDoc.title: Verify a deed copy
verifyDoc.intro: If someone gives you a copy of a deed, check whether it matches the recorded deed. We do not keep the file.

s1.title: Choose the copy
s1.body: On Verify a deed copy, press the file field. Use a phone photo or a PDF, up to 10 MB.
s1.alt: Verify a deed copy page with the file field outlined.

s2.title: Press Verify copy
s2.body: When the file name shows, press Verify copy. The answer comes within a minute.
s2.alt: Chosen file name and the Verify copy button outlined.

s3.title: Read the result
s3.body: If it does not match, the result lists what differs. Even on a match, confirm with the registry office.
s3.alt: Result card: the land area on the copy does not match the recorded deed.

map.title: Parcel map
map.intro: See plot boundaries with their dag and khatian numbers. Owner names are not shown here.

s1.title: Open the map
s1.body: Open Parcel map from the Services menu. You see the whole of Bangladesh.
s1.alt: Parcel map page with the map of Bangladesh outlined.

s2.title: Go to your area
s2.body: Press Show search menu. Pick the division, district and upazila. The map moves to that area.
s2.alt: Search menu with the division, district and upazila fields outlined.

s3.title: See the plot
s3.body: In the parcel list below the map, press Show on map. A small card shows the dag and khatian numbers.
s3.alt: A small card over a plot with its dag and khatian numbers.

authShell.panelBody: One secure account for citizens, reviewers and land office officers.

pageTip.title: What to do on this page?

verify.s1: Choose the district, upazila and mouza.
verify.s2: Type the khatian and dag numbers as they appear on your papers.
verify.s3: Press “Verify”. You need to sign in to see the full result.

check.s1: Enter the plot details of the land you want to buy.
check.s2: If you know the seller's name, add it as printed on the deed.
check.s3: Before you pay, take the list to a lawyer or the land office.

track.s1: Enter the application number from your receipt, e.g. MUT-2026-0001.
track.s2: Press “Track status” to see which step it has reached.
track.s3: If a hearing date is shown, go to the office that day with your papers.

verifyDoc.s1: Choose a photo or PDF of the deed copy you were given.
verifyDoc.s2: Press “Verify copy”. The file is not kept.
verifyDoc.s3: If any field does not match, check the original deed at the registry office.

my.s1: Pick a service from the three buttons at the top.
my.s2: Watch a plot to get a notice when something changes.
my.s3: Your past searches and reports are listed below.

officer.s1: The key numbers show how much work is waiting.
officer.s2: Open the oldest documents in the review list first.
officer.s3: Act on risk alerts. Dismiss a wrong alert with a reason.

reviewer.s1: Open the top document first. It has waited longest.
reviewer.s2: Compare every field read from the document with its image.
reviewer.s3: Approve if everything is right. Otherwise reject it with a reason.

upload.s1: Choose the document type. Add the land ID if you know it.
upload.s2: Pick the scanned file and press “Upload”.
upload.s3: Once it is read, the document goes to a reviewer's list.

mutations.s1: Use the tabs to pick applications by status.
mutations.s2: Use the area filter to see your office's applications.
mutations.s3: Open an application, read its pre-check, then decide.
